source: Bell et al. (2019), MNRAS 489, 1995, 'Mass loss from the exoplanet WASP-12b inferred from Spitzer phase curves' (doi:10.1093/mnras/stz2018; arXiv:1906.04742). Spitzer IRAC 3.6 um phase curve of 2013 (program 90186), the paper's fiducial analysis (M. Zhang's PLD pipeline, first-order sinusoid). Values read from the authors' LaTeX source: the phase-variation equations of section 3.1 and Table A2, 3.6 um rows.

radiusRatio.where: Table A2, 2013, A2 PLD 1st Order, R_p/R_*

eclipseDepth.cell: 3840 +/- 120 ppm, corrected for dilution from WASP-12BC
eclipseDepth.where: Table A2, 2013, A2 PLD 1st Order, F_day/F_*

model.equation: F_p(t) = F_day Phi(psi), Phi = 1 + C1 (cos psi - 1) + D1 sin psi, psi = 2 pi (t - t_e)/P counted from mid-eclipse (section 3.1). The fiducial 3.6 um model is first order: C2 and D2 are not fitted.

c1.where: Table A2, 2013, A2 PLD 1st Order, C_1

d1.where: Table A2, 2013, A2 PLD 1st Order, D_1

daysideK.where: Table A2, 2013, A2 PLD 1st Order, T_b,day

nightsideK.where: Table A2, 2013, A2 PLD 1st Order, T_b,night (appendix B: from F_day (1 - 2 C_1))

offsetDegrees.cell: 13.6 +/- 3.8 degrees after eclipse: the peak comes 13.6 degrees after eclipse, a hot spot west of noon
offsetDegrees.where: Table A2, 2013, A2 PLD 1st Order, 1st Order Phase Offset (degrees after eclipse)

notStated: The 3.6 um stellar brightness temperature behind Table A2. Appendix B gives 5,800 K at 3.6 um and 6,000 K at 4.5 um, but the 3.6 um rows follow about 6,030 K and the 4.5 um rows follow 5,800 K: the two appear swapped in the text. Through 5,800 K this row's day side would be 2,734 K, not the table's 2,813 K. The lens uses the value the table's own day side implies.
